```{r setup}
#| include: false

source("R/00_helpers.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ggplot2)
})

S   <- readRDS("summary/nh_sgp_summary.rds")
W   <- readRDS("summary/nh_wida_summary.rds")
ov  <- as.data.table(S$overall)
lev <- as.data.table(S$levels)
sg  <- as.data.table(S$subgroups)
sgp_pool <- as.data.table(S$subgroups_pooled)
tg  <- as.data.table(S$targets)
tgp <- as.data.table(S$targets_prior)
prof <- as.data.table(S$proficiency)
sgpd <- as.data.table(S$sgp_distribution)
M   <- S$meta
WM  <- W$meta
BNY <- if (!is.null(M$baseline_norm_year)) M$baseline_norm_year else "2018_2019"
BNYL <- pretty_year(BNY)

AY  <- M$analysis_year
AYL <- M$analysis_year_label
if (is.null(M$data_received) || !nzchar(M$data_received)) {
  M$data_received <- "July 9, 2026"
}

WAY <- WM$analysis_year
WAYL <- WM$analysis_year_label

COHORT_COL   <- "#3498DB"
BASELINE_COL <- "#E67E22"
LEVEL_COLS   <- c(Low = "#C0392B", Typical = "#95A5A6", High = "#27AE60")
GRID_COL     <- "#D8D8D4"
TEXT_COL     <- "#141410"
WIDA_COL     <- "#8E44AD"

theme_nh <- function(base_size = 22) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Noto Sans") +
    theme(
      text            = element_text(color = TEXT_COL),
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.05)),
      plot.subtitle   = element_text(color = "#5c5c58"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = GRID_COL, linewidth = 0.4),
      strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title    = element_blank(),
      axis.title      = element_text(color = "#5c5c58")
    )
}

mmn_cell <- function(content, grade_label, norm = c("cohort", "baseline"), year = AY) {
  norm <- match.arg(norm)
  r <- ov[CONTENT_AREA == content & GRADE_LABEL == grade_label & YEAR == year]
  if (!nrow(r) || (norm == "cohort" && is.na(r$n_cohort))) return("&mdash;")
  if (norm == "cohort") fmt_mmn(r$mean_cohort, r$median_cohort, r$n_cohort)
  else fmt_mmn(r$mean_baseline, r$median_baseline, r$n_baseline)
}

wida_mmn <- function(grade_label, norm = c("cohort", "baseline")) {
  norm <- match.arg(norm)
  r <- as.data.table(W$sgp_overall)[GRADE_LABEL == grade_label]
  if (!nrow(r)) return("&mdash;")
  if (norm == "cohort") fmt_mmn(r$mean_cohort, r$median_cohort, r$n_cohort)
  else fmt_mmn(r$mean_baseline, r$median_baseline, r$n_baseline)
}

fmt_mmsn <- function(mean_val, median_val, sd_val, n) {
  if (length(n) && !is.na(n) && n < SMALL_N) return("&mdash;")
  if (any(is.na(c(mean_val, median_val, sd_val, n)))) return("&mdash;")
  paste0(formatC(round(mean_val, 1), format = "f", digits = 1), "/",
         formatC(round(median_val, 0), format = "d"), "/",
         formatC(round(sd_val, 1), format = "f", digits = 1), "/",
         fmt_count(n))
}

get_val <- function(content, grade_label, col, year = AY) {
  r <- ov[CONTENT_AREA == content & GRADE_LABEL == grade_label & YEAR == year]
  if (!nrow(r)) return(NA_real_)
  r[[col]]
}

gof_token <- function(content_area) {
  data.table::fcase(
    content_area == "READING",     "ELA",
    content_area == "ELA",         "ELA",
    content_area == "MATHEMATICS", "MATH",
    default = content_area
  )
}

gof_src <- function(content_area, grade, year, norm = "cohort") {
  file.path("Figures", "gof",
            sprintf("%s_%s_%s_g%s.svg", gof_token(content_area), year, norm, grade))
}

wida_gof_src <- function(grade, year = WAY, norm = "baseline") {
  file.path("Figures", "gof", sprintf("wida_%s_%s_g%s.svg", year, norm, grade))
}

gof_figure <- function(content_area, grade, year, norm = "cohort",
                       caption = NULL, alt = NULL, max_height = NULL,
                       src = NULL) {
  if (is.null(src)) src <- gof_src(content_area, grade, year, norm)
  if (!file.exists(src)) {
    return(sprintf('<div style="padding:1em;color:#c0392b;font-size:0.6em">missing: %s</div>', src))
  }
  if (is.null(caption)) caption <- sprintf("%s Grade %s &mdash; %s (%s)",
                                           pretty_subject(content_area), pretty_grade(grade),
                                           pretty_year(year), norm)
  if (is.null(alt)) alt <- gsub("&mdash;", "-", caption)
  img_style <- if (!is.null(max_height)) {
    sprintf("max-height:%s;width:auto;max-width:100%%;display:block;margin:0 auto", max_height)
  } else {
    "width:100%;height:auto"
  }
  sprintf(
    '<figure style="margin:0;text-align:center">
       <img src="%s" alt="%s" style="%s"/>
       <figcaption>%s</figcaption>
     </figure>', src, alt, img_style, caption)
}

emit_html <- function(x) cat("\n```{=html}\n", x, "\n```\n", sep = "")

gof_grid <- function(figs, min_col = "300px", gap = "0.6em", class = NULL) {
  class_attr <- if (!is.null(class)) sprintf(' class="%s"', class) else ""
  emit_html(sprintf(
    '<div%s style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(%s,1fr));gap:%s;align-items:start">%s</div>',
    class_attr, min_col, gap, paste(figs, collapse = "")))
}

table_css <- sprintf('
<style>
  table.results-table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%%; font-size: 0.72em; }
  table.results-table th, table.results-table td { padding: 0.35em 0.6em; text-align: center; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-border); }
  table.results-table thead .grp { font-family: "Josefin Sans", sans-serif; font-weight: 600; }
  table.results-table thead .grp-ela  { color: %s; border-bottom: 2px solid %s; }
  table.results-table thead .grp-math { color: %s; border-bottom: 2px solid %s; }
  table.results-table .rt-grade { text-align: left; font-family: "Josefin Sans", sans-serif; }
  table.results-table .rt-base { color: %s; }
  table.results-table tbody tr:hover { background: var(--color-surface-subtle); }
  table.results-table tr.dim-row th { text-align:left; background: var(--color-surface-subtle);
    font-family:"Josefin Sans",sans-serif; color: var(--color-primary); padding-top:0.5em; }
  .rt-caption { font-size: 0.55em; color: var(--color-secondary); font-style: italic; margin-top: 0.4em; }
</style>', COHORT_COL, COHORT_COL, "#7a5c33", "#7a5c33", BASELINE_COL)
```

# SGP results for 2026 {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section one: 2026 NH SAS results
:::


## What was run: NH SAS (grades 4&ndash;8)

Two SGP analyses were conducted on the `r AYL` NH SAS data (ELA and Mathematics, grades 3&ndash;8; growth from grade 4):

- **Cohort-referenced** &mdash; growth norms built from the most recent cohorts; by construction these center mean/median SGP on **50**.
- **Baseline-referenced** &mdash; historical coefficient matrices from the pre-pandemic **2018&ndash;19** administration (with 2017&ndash;18 priors). These are **not** centered on 50 and let us examine COVID-era academic recovery, changes in rates of learning, and possible **scale drift**.
- **Projections** (lagged and straight, three-year catch-up / keep-up and move-up / stay-up) were calculated using both norm sets.

Science and grade 11 are on the file but are **not** included in the SGP analyses.

::: {.key-insight}
Cohort norms answer *"how did this student grow relative to academic peers this year?"* Baseline norms answer *"how does that growth compare to pre-pandemic rates of learning?"*
:::

::: {.notes}
Same 2018-19 baseline window New Hampshire has used since the skip-year 2020-21 analyses. Grade 3 has no prior, so no SGP. SCIENCE and grade 11 are INVALID_CASE in the prep scripts.
:::


## Provenance &amp; reproducibility {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
- NH SAS analyses used student-level data supplied by the New Hampshire Department of Education, **received `r M$data_received`**.
- WIDA ACCESS analyses used the ESOL extract for 2026 (with both the new and old composite scales).
- Conducted with the **`SGP` R package** (version `r M$sgp_package_version`).
- All analyses converged; goodness-of-fit plots confirm successful analyses.

## Reading the 2026 baseline results

```{r baseline-narrative}
#| output: asis

by <- ov[YEAR == AY & !is.na(n_baseline) & n_baseline > 0]
by[, dev := mean_baseline - 50]
flag <- by[!is.na(dev) & abs(dev) >= 2][order(-abs(dev))]

mk <- function(x) sprintf("%s Grade %s (mean <strong>%.1f</strong>)",
                          x$SUBJECT, x$GRADE_LABEL, x$mean_baseline)
li <- function(dt) {
  if (!nrow(dt)) return("<li>None materially different</li>")
  paste0("<li>", vapply(seq_len(nrow(dt)), function(i) mk(dt[i]), character(1)), "</li>", collapse = "")
}
above <- flag[dev > 0]; below <- flag[dev < 0]

emit_html(sprintf('
<div style="display:flex;gap:2em;align-items:flex-start">
  <div style="flex:1">
    <p style="font-weight:600;color:#27ae60;margin-bottom:0.2em">Above pre-pandemic rates (baseline mean &gt; 52)</p>
    <ul>%s</ul>
  </div>
  <div style="flex:1">
    <p style="font-weight:600;color:#c0392b;margin-bottom:0.2em">Below pre-pandemic rates (baseline mean &lt; 48)</p>
    <ul>%s</ul>
  </div>
</div>', li(above), li(below)))
```

::: {.key-insight}
Cohort-referenced results are, as expected, centered on 50 with even conditional coverage. The **baseline** results are the diagnostic lens &mdash; they say whether `r AYL` growth matches the 2018&ndash;19 rate of learning.
:::

::: {.notes}
Generated from the cache, so the flagged grades update automatically. Keep interpretation cautious here; the trend slide does the interpreting.
:::


## Growth distribution: Low / Typical / High

```{r level-distribution}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.2

ld <- lev[YEAR == AY & !is.na(LEVEL) & GRADE_LABEL %in% as.character(4:8)]
ld[, GRADE_LABEL := factor(GRADE_LABEL, levels = as.character(4:8))]
ld[, NORM := factor(NORM, levels = c("Cohort", "Baseline"))]

ggplot(ld, aes(x = GRADE_LABEL, y = pct, fill = LEVEL)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.78) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(33.3, 66.7), color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "22") +
  facet_grid(SUBJECT ~ NORM) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = LEVEL_COLS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = paste0("Share of students at each growth level, ", AYL),
       subtitle = "Cohort norms split roughly one-third each; baseline shifts reveal recovery / drift") +
  theme_nh(20)
```

::: {.notes}
Cohort panels should show the classic ~1/3 Low, Typical, High. Where baseline panels tilt toward Low or High is where pre-pandemic-referenced growth diverges.
:::


# Model fit and conditional coverage {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section two: model fit
:::


## What these plots do and do not diagnose

Each plot shows, for every decile of prior achievement, the share of students falling in each growth-percentile decile. Two different things move those cells, and only one of them is a fitting problem.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**What they diagnose**

*Systematic tilt across prior achievement.* If growth percentiles drift upward or downward as prior achievement rises, the conditional model is not covering the range of prior achievement evenly. That is misfit, and it is actionable.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**What they cannot diagnose**

*Departure from exact uniformity.* Scores are discrete. Students sharing a prior and a current score must receive the same growth percentile, so the conditional distribution cannot be uniform and the cells cannot all sit at 10%. That lumpiness follows from fitting a continuous quantile model to a discrete scale.
:::
:::

::: {.key-insight}
The diagnostic content is the **tilt**, not the distance from 10%. For baseline norms a level shift is neither misfit nor uniformity: it is the change in the prior-to-current relationship that the comparison exists to detect.
:::

::: {.notes}
Same framing as the Rhode Island TAC deck. What remains diagnostic is conditional tilt.
:::

# Growth in context {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section three: pandemic context
:::


## Where were they during the pandemic?

The `r AYL` tested grades sat in very different places when schooling was disrupted. There is no `2019_2020` NH SAS administration.

```{r pandemic-table}
#| output: asis

rows <- c(
  '<tr><th class="rt-grade">Grade 8</th><td>Grade 2</td><td>Grade 3</td></tr>',
  '<tr><th class="rt-grade">Grade 7</th><td>Grade 1</td><td>Grade 2</td></tr>',
  '<tr><th class="rt-grade">Grade 6</th><td>Kindergarten</td><td>Grade 1</td></tr>',
  '<tr><th class="rt-grade">Grade 5</th><td>Pre-K</td><td>Kindergarten</td></tr>',
  '<tr><th class="rt-grade">Grade 4</th><td>Not yet in school</td><td>Pre-K</td></tr>'
)
emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.7em;max-width:75%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade in %s</th><th>Spring 2020</th><th>2020&ndash;21 (first post-COVID test)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Grade 8 in %s spent early-elementary years in disrupted schooling; grade 4 had not yet entered the tested progression.</div>',
AYL, paste(rows, collapse = ""), AYL)))
```

::: {.notes}
The point is only to locate the 2026 grades in the pandemic, not to claim a causal reading of any one cell.
:::


## Trend: same grade over time (baseline SGP)

```{r baseline-trend}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.0

tr <- ov[GRADE_LABEL %in% as.character(4:8) &
         YEAR %in% c("2021_2022","2022_2023","2023_2024","2024_2025","2025_2026") &
         !is.na(mean_baseline)]
tr[, GRADE_LABEL := factor(paste("Grade", GRADE_LABEL), levels = paste("Grade", 4:8))]
tr[, YEAR_LABEL := factor(YEAR_LABEL, levels = as.character(2022:2026))]

ggplot(tr, aes(x = YEAR_LABEL, y = mean_baseline, color = SUBJECT, group = SUBJECT)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 50, color = "#9a9a94", linetype = "22") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ GRADE_LABEL, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(ELA = COHORT_COL, Mathematics = "#7a5c33")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean baseline SGP",
       title = "Same-grade baseline-referenced growth, 2022–2026",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = the 2018–19 rate of learning. A return toward 50 is recovery completing, not a new decline.") +
  theme_nh(18)
```

::: {.notes}
Read each panel as a fixed grade across years, not a cohort aging. Mathematics returning toward 50 is the fading of rebound growth; a line that stays below 50 is the genuine concern.
:::

:::


# Growth equity {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section four: growth by student group
:::


## Growth by student group (NH SAS, `r AYL`)

```{r equity-table}
#| output: asis

dims <- c("English Learner", "Students w/ Disability", "Economically Disadv.")
sp <- sgp_pool[DIMENSION %in% dims]

cell <- function(subj, grp, col) {
  r <- sp[SUBJECT == subj & GROUP == grp]
  if (!nrow(r)) return("&mdash;")
  fmt_mmsn(r[[paste0("mean_", col)]], r[[paste0("median_", col)]],
           r[[paste0("sd_", col)]], r[[paste0("n_", col)]])
}

body <- ""
for (d in dims) {
  grps <- sp[DIMENSION == d, unique(GROUP)]
  body <- paste0(body, sprintf('<tr class="dim-row"><th colspan="5">%s</th></tr>', d))
  for (grp in grps) {
    body <- paste0(body, sprintf(
      '<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td class="rt-base">%s</td><td>%s</td><td class="rt-base">%s</td></tr>',
      grp, cell("ELA", grp, "cohort"), cell("ELA", grp, "baseline"),
      cell("Mathematics", grp, "cohort"), cell("Mathematics", grp, "baseline")))
  }
}

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.62em">
  <thead>
    <tr><th rowspan="2">Group</th>
        <th class="grp grp-ela" colspan="2">ELA</th>
        <th class="grp grp-math" colspan="2">Mathematics</th></tr>
    <tr><th>Cohort</th><th class="rt-base">Baseline</th><th>Cohort</th><th class="rt-base">Baseline</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">mean&#8202;/&#8202;median&#8202;/&#8202;SD&#8202;/&#8202;N, NH SAS grades 4&ndash;8 pooled, %s. Cells with N &lt; 10 are suppressed.</div>', body, AYL)))
```

::: {.notes}
SDs travel with the means. If every group sits near the same SD, the equity story is entirely in central tendency.
:::

## Equity gaps at a glance

```{r equity-plot}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6.0

dims <- c("English Learner", "Students w/ Disability", "Economically Disadv.")
ep <- sgp_pool[DIMENSION %in% dims & !is.na(mean_cohort),
               .(mean_sgp = weighted.mean(mean_cohort, n_cohort, na.rm = TRUE),
                 mean_base = weighted.mean(mean_baseline, n_baseline, na.rm = TRUE)),
               by = .(DIMENSION, GROUP)]
epl <- melt(ep, id.vars = c("DIMENSION","GROUP"),
            measure.vars = c("mean_sgp","mean_base"),
            variable.name = "norm", value.name = "sgp")
epl[, norm := factor(norm, labels = c("Cohort", "Baseline"))]

ggplot(epl, aes(x = sgp, y = reorder(GROUP, sgp), fill = norm)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, color = "#9a9a94", linetype = "22") +
  facet_wrap(~ DIMENSION, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Cohort = COHORT_COL, Baseline = BASELINE_COL)) +
  labs(x = "Mean SGP (ELA + Mathematics pooled)", y = NULL,
       title = paste0("Growth by student group, ", AYL)) +
  theme_nh(19)
```

::: {.notes}
Dashed line is 50. Cohort bars near 50 = comparable current-year growth. Descriptive, not causal.
:::


## Within-year growth is close to comparable across groups

```{r equity-comparable}
#| output: asis

pairs <- list(
  c("Female", "Male"),
  c("English Learners (EL)", "Non-English Learners (Non-EL)"),
  c("Students with Disabilities (SWD)", "Students without Disabilities (Non-SWD)"),
  c("Economically Disadvantaged", "Not Economically Disadvantaged")
)
labs_ <- c("Gender (Female vs Male)", "English learners", "Students with disabilities", "Economically disadvantaged")

mk <- function(pr, lab) {
  vals <- vapply(c("ELA", "Mathematics"), function(sj) {
    a <- sgp_pool[SUBJECT == sj & GROUP == pr[1], mean_cohort]
    b <- sgp_pool[SUBJECT == sj & GROUP == pr[2], mean_cohort]
    if (!length(a) || !length(b) || is.na(a) || is.na(b)) return("&mdash;")
    sprintf("%.1f vs %.1f", a, b)
  }, character(1))
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', lab, vals[1], vals[2])
}

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.68em;max-width:70%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Group vs. comparison group</th><th>ELA</th><th>Mathematics</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Mean cohort-referenced SGP, NH SAS grades 4&ndash;8 pooled, %s.</div>',
paste(vapply(seq_along(pairs), function(i) mk(pairs[[i]], labs_[i]), character(1)), collapse = ""), AYL)))
```

::: {.key-insight}
Where achievement gaps are large, **within-year growth is often not**. Cohort SGPs near 50 for both members of a pair mean the gap is being maintained rather than widened this year.
:::

::: {.notes}
Descriptive. Name the pair that is not close, if any, as the priority.
:::


# Target attainment {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section five: catch-up / keep-up
:::


## What the target actually is

"Catch up" and "keep up" mean nothing without a stated horizon. In New Hampshire the NH SAS target is proficiency **by the end of the grades 3&ndash;8 progression**, so the horizon shrinks as students approach grade 8.

```{r targets-horizon}
#| output: asis

hz <- tg[METRIC == "Catch Up / Keep Up" & NORM == "Cohort",
         .(n = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE), attained = sum(attained, na.rm = TRUE),
           yrs = suppressWarnings(max(years_to_target, na.rm = TRUE))),
         by = .(GRADE_LABEL, aspiration)]
hz[, rate := 100 * attained / n]

grades_h <- as.character(4:8)
rows_h <- vapply(grades_h, function(gl) {
  cu <- hz[GRADE_LABEL == gl & aspiration == "Catch Up"]
  ku <- hz[GRADE_LABEL == gl & aspiration == "Keep Up"]
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">Grade %s</th><td><strong>%s</strong></td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
          gl,
          if (nrow(cu) && is.finite(cu$yrs)) ifelse(cu$yrs == 0, "same year",
            sprintf("%d year%s", as.integer(cu$yrs), ifelse(cu$yrs == 1, "", "s"))) else "&mdash;",
          if (nrow(cu) && !is.na(cu$rate)) sprintf("%.1f%%", cu$rate) else "&mdash;",
          if (nrow(ku) && !is.na(ku$rate)) sprintf("%.1f%%", ku$rate) else "&mdash;")
}, character(1))

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.66em;max-width:70%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade</th><th>Horizon to target</th><th>Catch-up rate</th><th>Keep-up rate</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Cohort targets, NH SAS, ELA and mathematics pooled, %s. Horizon is the median number of years to the target.</div>',
paste(rows_h, collapse = ""), AYL)))
```

::: {.key-insight}
As the horizon shrinks, catch-up rates fall and keep-up rates rise. Most of the apparent grade gradient is the **target**, not the students.
:::

::: {.notes}
Grade 8 "catch up" collapses into "is proficient now." Grade-to-grade comparisons are not meaningful unless the horizon travels with them.
:::


## Catch-up / keep-up attainment (NH SAS, `r AYL`)

```{r targets-plot}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 5.9

ct <- tg[METRIC == "Catch Up / Keep Up" & NORM == "Cohort" & !is.na(rate)]
ct[, GRADE_LABEL := factor(GRADE_LABEL, levels = as.character(4:8))]
ct[, aspiration := factor(aspiration, levels = c("Catch Up", "Keep Up"))]
ct[, xlab := paste0(GRADE_LABEL, "\n(", ifelse(is.na(years_to_target) | years_to_target == 0, "same yr",
                    paste0(years_to_target, " yr")), ")")]
ct <- ct[order(GRADE_LABEL)]
ct[, xlab := factor(xlab, levels = unique(xlab))]

ggplot(ct, aes(x = xlab, y = rate, fill = aspiration)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.68) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = rate_lo, ymax = rate_hi),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.16,
                linewidth = 0.5, color = "#141410") +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_count(n), y = 3),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 3.6, color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ SUBJECT) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Catch Up" = "#8E44AD", "Keep Up" = COHORT_COL)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Grade (horizon to target)", y = "% attaining target",
       title = "Share of students on track to catch up / keep up",
       subtitle = "Catch Up = students below proficient; Keep Up = students at/above.\nBars show 95% Wilson intervals; N is printed in each bar.") +
  theme_nh(19)
```

::: {.notes}
Read across grades only with the horizon in view. Intervals are here so the rates are falsifiable.
:::


## Target attainment by prior achievement

```{r targets-prior}
#| output: asis

th <- tgp[NORM == "Cohort" & !is.na(rate)]
low  <- th[ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL_PRIOR %in% c("Below Proficient") & aspiration == "Catch Up"]
high <- th[ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL_PRIOR %in% c("Above Proficient") & aspiration == "Keep Up"]

low_rate  <- if (nrow(low))  weighted.mean(low$rate,  low$n)  else NA_real_
high_rate <- if (nrow(high)) weighted.mean(high$rate, high$n) else NA_real_
low_n  <- if (nrow(low))  sum(low$n)  else 0
high_n <- if (nrow(high)) sum(high$n) else 0

emit_html(sprintf('
<div style="display:flex;gap:2em;justify-content:center;margin-top:0.5em">
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s</div>
    <div class="stat-label">of students who were <strong>Below Proficient</strong> last year<br/>are on track to <strong>catch up</strong><br/>
      <span style="font-size:0.82em;opacity:0.75">N = %s</span></div></div>
  <div class="stat-callout"><div class="stat-number">%s</div>
    <div class="stat-label">of students who were <strong>Above Proficient</strong> last year<br/>are on track to <strong>keep up</strong><br/>
      <span style="font-size:0.82em;opacity:0.75">N = %s</span></div></div>
</div>
<div class="rt-caption" style="text-align:center">These are different students judged against different targets, so the two figures are not a gap. NH SAS, ELA and mathematics pooled, %s.</div>',
fmt_pct(low_rate), fmt_count(low_n), fmt_pct(high_rate), fmt_count(high_n), AYL))
```

::: {.key-insight}
Students entering below proficient face the steepest catch-up targets and attain them least often &mdash; the central equity concern for accountability use of these growth results.
:::

::: {.notes}
Say the caveat out loud: these two percentages describe different students measured against different targets.
:::


# WIDA ACCESS for New Hampshire {.center}

::: {.visually-hidden}
Section six: WIDA ACCESS
:::


## What was run: WIDA ACCESS

English learners in New Hampshire take ACCESS for ELLs. The SGP analyses treat the Overall ELP composite as `READING` and ask whether students are **on track to the state's exit standard**.

- **Exit / proficiency criterion:** **WIDA Level 4.5** (in `SGPstateData` and in the prep scripts since 2019). Fine-grained scores 4.5&ndash;4.9 are collapsed to Level 4.5.
- **Cohort SGPs** for 2026 were computed on the **new ACCESS 3.0 scale**.
- **Baseline SGPs and baseline catch-up / keep-up targets** were computed on the **old ACCESS 2.0 scale**, against the existing 4.5 cuts. Those are the headline on-track results in this section.
- Targets run 1 to 6 years forward. The rates below use the **6-year** horizon &mdash; the longest window present in the object.

::: {.warning-box}
::: {.warning-box-title}
2026 is a transition year
:::
`WIDA_NH` does not yet carry the consortium's 2026 transition metadata (new cuts, knots, linkages). Cohort targets computed on the new scale against old-scale cuts are not on the same footing as the baseline targets. They are shown only as a discussion item.
:::

::: {.notes}
Be explicit: 4.5, not 4.7. New Mexico uses 4.7; New Hampshire does not. The 2026 script swapped SCALE_SCORE and SCALE_SCORE_OLD_SCALE so baseline ran on the old scale, then swapped back.
:::


## ACCESS participation by grade, `r WAYL`

```{r wida-participation}
#| output: asis

pt <- as.data.table(W$participation)[YEAR == WAY]
pt <- pt[order(as.numeric(GRADE))]
rows <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pt)), function(i) {
  r <- pt[i]
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
          r$GRADE_LABEL, fmt_count(r$n_tested),
          fmt_count(r$n_growth_cohort), fmt_count(r$n_growth_baseline))
}, character(1))

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.62em;max-width:70%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade</th><th>N tested</th><th>N with cohort SGP</th><th class="rt-base">N with baseline SGP</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">WIDA ACCESS Overall ELP, %s. Kindergarten is shown as K. Cells with N &lt; 10 are suppressed later in the on-track tables, not here.</div>',
paste(rows, collapse = ""), WAYL)))
```

::: {.notes}
Kindergarten has no prior, so no SGP. Upper-grade cells are smaller; that is why the on-track tables suppress N < 10.
:::


## The 2026 scale transition

```{r wida-scale}
#| output: asis

st <- as.data.table(W$scale_transition)
st <- st[order(as.numeric(GRADE))]
rows <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(st)), function(i) {
  r <- st[i]
  sprintf(
    '<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
    r$GRADE_LABEL,
    fmt_count(r$n),
    if (is.na(r$cor_new_old)) "&mdash;" else sprintf("%.2f", r$cor_new_old),
    if (is.na(r$mean_diff)) "&mdash;" else sprintf("%+.1f", r$mean_diff),
    if (is.na(r$pct_proficient_reported)) "&mdash;" else sprintf("%.1f%%", r$pct_proficient_reported),
    if (is.na(r$pct_proficient_old_cuts)) "&mdash;" else sprintf("%.1f%%", r$pct_proficient_old_cuts)
  )
}, character(1))

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.58em">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Grade</th><th>N</th><th>r (new, old)</th><th>Mean (new &minus; old)</th>
      <th>%% at/above 4.5<br/>(reported, new scale)</th>
      <th>%% at/above 4.5<br/>(old scale, 4.5 cuts)</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Old-scale percent proficient reapplies the current WIDA_NH Level 4.5 cuts to SCALE_SCORE_OLD_SCALE. The two percent-proficient columns are not interchangeable.</div>',
paste(rows, collapse = ""))))
```

::: {.key-insight}
The 2026 file carries both composites for every tested student. That is what makes an old-scale baseline analysis possible in the transition year, and what makes a silent mix of the two scales a mistake.
:::

::: {.notes}
If the two percent-proficient columns diverge, that is the transition, not a change in the students.
:::

## On track by current WIDA level

```{r wida-ontrack-level}
#| output: asis

ol <- as.data.table(W$on_track_level)[!is.na(rate) & aspiration == "Catch Up"]
ol[, ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL := factor(as.character(ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL), levels = WIDA_LEVELS)]
setorder(ol, ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL)

rows <- ""
for (lv in WIDA_LEVELS) {
  cu <- ol[ACHIEVEMENT_LEVEL == lv]
  if (!nrow(cu)) next
  rows <- paste0(rows, sprintf(
    '<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
    pretty_wida_level(lv),
    fmt_pct(cu$rate, 1),
    fmt_count(cu$n)
  ))
}

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.64em;max-width:62%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Current level</th><th>Catch-up rate</th><th>N</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Baseline 6-year catch-up, old scale, %s. The 6-year CUKU column codes students who started the window below 4.5; students already at the exit standard do not receive a 6-year Keep Up status. Cells with N &lt; 10 are suppressed.</div>',
rows, WAYL)))
```

::: {.notes}
Students currently at Level 4 are nearest the 4.5 exit; students at Level 1 face the longest catch-up. A student now at 4.5+ with a Catch Up status reached the exit during the window.
:::


## Years to the Level 4.5 target

```{r wida-ytt}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 5.8

yt <- as.data.table(W$years_to_target)[!is.na(pct) & GRADE_LABEL %in% as.character(1:8)]
yt[, GRADE_F := factor(paste("Grade", GRADE_LABEL), levels = paste("Grade", 1:8))]

ggplot(yt, aes(x = factor(years), y = pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = WIDA_COL, width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~ GRADE_F, nrow = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Years to Level 4.5 (baseline, 6-year configuration)",
       y = NULL,
       title = "Distribution of years-to-target, grades 1–8",
       subtitle = paste0("From ", WM$cuku_baseline_column, " / ", WM$cuku_horizon,
                         "-year configuration. Zero = already at or above the exit standard.")) +
  theme_nh(17)
```

::: {.notes}
Zero years = already proficient. A pile-up at 6 years means the 6-year window is still not enough for those students.
:::


## Cohort vs. baseline on-track &mdash; a discussion item

```{r wida-compare}
#| output: asis

oc <- as.data.table(W$on_track_compare)[!is.na(rate) & aspiration == "Catch Up"]
oc[, GRADE_LABEL := factor(GRADE_LABEL, levels = c("K", as.character(1:12)))]
grades <- levels(oc$GRADE_LABEL)
grades <- grades[grades %in% oc$GRADE_LABEL]

rows <- vapply(grades, function(gl) {
  b <- oc[GRADE_LABEL == gl & NORM == "Baseline"]
  c <- oc[GRADE_LABEL == gl & NORM == "Cohort"]
  sprintf('<tr><th class="rt-grade">%s</th><td class="rt-base">%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
          gl,
          if (nrow(b)) sprintf("%.1f%% (N = %s)", b$rate, fmt_count(b$n)) else "&mdash;",
          if (nrow(c)) sprintf("%.1f%% (N = %s)", c$rate, fmt_count(c$n)) else "&mdash;")
}, character(1))

emit_html(paste0(table_css, sprintf('
<div class="warning-box" style="margin-bottom:0.8em">
  <div class="warning-box-title">Do not treat these two columns as a trend</div>
  Baseline catch-up uses the old scale and the current 4.5 cuts. Cohort catch-up uses the new scale against those same old cuts. The difference is a scale-transition artefact until WIDA_NH carries 2026 transition metadata.
</div>
<table class="results-table" style="font-size:0.6em;max-width:70%%;margin:0 auto">
  <thead><tr><th>Grade</th><th class="rt-base">Baseline catch-up (old scale)</th><th>Cohort catch-up (new scale)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>%s</tbody>
</table>
<div class="rt-caption">Catch Up only, 6-year horizon, %s. Keep-up rates omitted here so the contrast is readable.</div>',
paste(rows, collapse = ""), WAYL)))
```

::: {.notes}
This is the TAC discussion item. Recommend reporting baseline on-track only for 2026, and deciding whether WIDA_NH should adopt the consortium 2026 cuts/knots/linkages now or wait for the new standards.
:::

:::


## Summary {.smaller}

- **NH SAS cohort SGPs** show even conditional coverage across grades 4&ndash;8 in ELA and mathematics &mdash; suitable for accountability calculations.
- **NH SAS baseline SGPs** are the diagnostic lens on recovery relative to 2018&ndash;19. Grades flagged more than two points from 50 are listed on the baseline-results slide.
- **Within-year growth is close to comparable across student groups**; where it is not, that pair is the priority.
- **Catch-up / keep-up rates are not comparable across grades** without their target horizon, which shrinks toward grade 8.
- **WIDA ACCESS exit remains WIDA Level 4.5.** Headline on-track results are **baseline-referenced and computed on the old composite scale**.
- **2026 is an ACCESS 3.0 transition year.** Cohort targets on the new scale against old cuts should not be reported as a trend. Whether `WIDA_NH` adopts the consortium's 2026 transition metadata is a TAC question.

::: {.notes}
Land the two programmes separately. The WIDA transition is the one that needs a decision.
:::


## Questions for the TAC {.smaller}

::: {.key-insight-box}
::: {.key-insight-box-title}
Where the committee's guidance is needed
:::
1. **How long should New Hampshire carry the old-scale WIDA baseline** after ACCESS 3.0? The 2026 split run is possible only because both composites are on the file.
2. **Should `WIDA_NH` adopt the consortium 2026 transition metadata now** (cuts, knots, linkages already on the generic `WIDA` entry), or wait until new standards are set?
3. **Should 2026 cohort on-track results be withheld** from public reporting, the way a contradicted baseline series would be, until the new-scale cuts exist?
4. **Should the 2018&ndash;19 NH SAS baseline continue** as the monitoring series, or is it time to discuss a dual track &mdash; a fixed recovery series plus a re-established reporting norm?
:::

::: {.notes}
Leave this up and open the floor. Questions 1-3 are WIDA; question 4 is NH SAS. This deck takes a position on 2026 WIDA reporting (baseline / old scale / 4.5) and asks the committee to confirm it.
:::
